This is true. It's a pain to have to maintain a store and the books. As @clamhurt_legbeard say's, store hours are required, and I've known several people who've done this, however, setting up a business in your home and maintaining the hours is something most don't want to deal with. Also, you are a business, so there's tax implications, both State and Federal, as well as State, County, sometime local regs you have to adhere to, too. Lots of hoops to jump through.

BTW, personally I have an FFL, but it's a Curio & Relic {C&R) FFL. That permits me to buy anything fifty years or older (much of what I prefer anyway) using it. I can buy anything considered C&R via the mail, from places like Gunbroker.com, etc. All I need do is send them a copy of my license and pat shipping.

The drawbacks are that 1) I am not permitted to sell, as a collector, I can sell guns from my collection, but I can't operate it as a business. So you're limited, they expect if you sell, it's to benefit your collection, not to profit. 2) The license is tied to my home address, so you'll likely need to have a permanent address where you're stable. I can't transfer it to a new address, I have to apply for a new license. 3) I have to keep a bound book (paper) of all my purchases, and the ATF can request to visit me and see it at any time. They do set up an appointment though, and unlike a full FFL, no surprises. I can also opt to meet at their local offices. 4) You have to notify your local Police Chief or Sheriff, whoever is the head E of your area in writing that you have it and collect firearms. On the good side, the local LE has no say in the process, it's a notification thing only and you are just required to notify them in writing, they have no yes or no vote on whether you get it.

The plus are 1) The license is inexpensive ... I can't recall off the top of my head, but like thirty dollars and valid for 3 years. 2) It's easily renewed, just send them another thirty, with a filled out form, and you get a renewal in the mail. 3) If you can pass a background check to buy a gun now, and meet a few minor requirements, you'll get the C&R FFL issued. 3) Gives me the freedom to buy (or sell) online without a hassle. No fees, no problems, a package just arrives at my door.

I like mine, and have used it often over the years. But if you're paranoid about the ATF or local LE knowing you collect guns, it's not for you.
